newsitem.title: UK: UK house prices to rise 3.4 pct over year - agents.
newsitem.headline: UK house prices to rise 3.4 pct over year - agents.

text.p: Estate agents see a 3.4 percent rise in UK house prices over the next 12 months, Birmingham Midshires Building Society said on Tuesday.
Prices should be fuelled by a shortage of properties coming on to the market, the UK's tenth largest building society said in a survey of 300 estate agents carried out with polling organisation ICM.
"Demand for homes is steadily increasing but there is still a shortage of properties on the market, which is pushing up prices," said Mike Jackson, chief executive.
The survey also showed that 83 percent of estate agents are now confident that the housing market is improving, an increase of 153 percent since the start of the year.
UBS recently raised its house price forecasts to seven percent for this year and 10 percent for 1997, citing a vigorous recovery in the housing market.
A Reuters survey of economists and mortgage lenders last week predicted a 4-1/2 percent increase in 1996 and a 6-1/2 percent increase in 1997.
House prices in London and south east England would continue to lead the way, with more modest increases in the north of England and Scotland, the survey said.
